# Project Intake

Everything below is what we ask before a scoping call. Every question exists because its answer
changes how we staff the team, how we scope the work, or what it costs. If a question does not
move one of those three, it is not on the form.

You can answer it in an email, a document, or on a call. There is no portal and no application
deadline.

::: {.callout-note}
**Short on time?** Answer sections 2, 3, and 8. Those are the ones that decide whether we can
help you and when we could start. We will fill in the rest on the call.
:::

## Before You Start: Two Rules Worth Knowing

**One engagement ships one product.** A dedicated two-person team at 640 hours can build and
ship one focused product. It cannot build two. If you have more than one project in mind, that
is welcome and common, but each is scoped, staffed, and priced as its own engagement. They can
run in parallel if the bench has room, or in sequence. Telling us about both up front is better
than compressing them into one brief.

**When AI influences a decision about a person, you own the decision.** We build hiring,
admissions, screening, and scoring tools, and we build them carefully. What we do not do is
certify that a scoring instrument is fair, valid, or legally defensible for employment or
admissions use. A human on your side reviews every output, your counsel owns validation, and we
put all of that in writing before the build phase starts.

## Section 1. Who You Are

1. Company name and website
2. Your name, title, email, and phone
3. Are you the person who can approve scope and budget? If not, who is?
4. How did you hear about us?

## Section 2. The Problem

5. In two or three sentences, what problem do you want solved?
6. What happens today, without this? Who does the work, and how?
7. How will you know it worked? Name the number that moves.
8. Have you tried to solve this before? What happened?

Question 8 matters more than it looks. A previous attempt that stalled is the best available
map of where the hard part actually is.

## Section 3. What You Want Built

9. Which best describes it? Select all that apply.
    - Net-new web or mobile application
    - AI agent or copilot over your own data
    - Automation of an existing workflow
    - Analytics, forecasting, or a decision model
    - Replacing a tool you currently pay for
    - Not sure yet, we want the audit
10. Who uses it, and roughly how many of them? Internal staff, your customers, the public?
11. Is there an existing product or vendor this replaces or sits next to? Name it.
12. If we shipped one thing in eight months, what is the single most important piece?
13. What is explicitly out of scope, as far as you are concerned?

Question 12 becomes the scope anchor. We quote your answer back to you in the written scope, so
answer it as though it were binding, because it largely is.

## Section 4. Technical Environment

14. Do you have engineers on staff? How many, and will any of them work with us?
15. What is your current stack and hosting, if any?
16. Who owns the code repository during the build, you or us?
17. List every system this must connect to, one per line.
18. Can you provision accounts and API access for the team within two weeks of kickoff?

Question 18 is the single most common cause of a stalled engagement. An honest "probably not"
is far more useful to us than an optimistic yes.

## Section 5. Data

19. What data will the team need to see?
20. Does any of it include personal information about identifiable individuals, health
    information, education records, records about minors, or payment and financial account
    data?
21. Is the data available today, or does it need to be collected or cleaned first?
22. Do you require your own NDA, or is our standard mutual NDA acceptable?

## Section 6. If AI Makes or Influences a Decision

Skip this section if it does not apply.

23. Will the system's output influence a decision about a person? Hiring, admission, credit,
    credentialing, care, or discipline?
24. If yes, who on your side reviews the output before the decision is made?
25. What does a wrong answer cost you?
26. Do you have labeled examples of good and bad outcomes we can learn from?

Question 26 decides whether a scoring model can be evaluated at all inside eight months. Without
labeled outcomes there is no way to tell a good score from a confident one.

## Section 7. Design

27. Do you have brand assets, a design system, or existing interfaces we should match?
28. Is design quality a priority here, or is this an internal tool where function is enough?

## Section 8. Timing, Budget, and Commitment

29. When would you want to start?
30. Is there a hard external deadline? What drives it?
31. Our standard engagement is $22,000 fixed for eight months, covering discovery, build, and
    transfer. Is that workable?
32. Who is your single weekly point of contact, and can they hold a standing 30 to 45 minute
    call?
33. Can you turn around decisions the team raises within one week?
34. May we name you publicly as a partner and use the work as a case study?

## Section 9. Anything Else

35. What have we not asked that we should have?
36. Attach anything useful: specs, screenshots, an RFP you already wrote.

## What Happens Next

| Step | When |
|---|---|
| We review for fit and reply | 2 business days |
| 45-minute scoping call | Week 1 |
| We name the proposed team and confirm the bench can staff it | Same week |
| Discovery scoped and confirmed in writing, with fee, IP, and confidentiality terms | Week 2 |
| Kickoff and architecture review | Week 3 |

We do not tell a student they are on your project before the scope is signed, and we do not
sign a build phase we cannot staff properly. If the answer is that we are not the right fit, you
will get that answer in the first week rather than the fourth.
